prepared_by: Codex collecting agent (single reviewer); independent reviewer assigned

vulnerability.title: Netty SnappyFrameDecoder neither caps compressed chunk size nor streaming-skips reserved skippable chunks, so malicious Snappy input can exhaust the decoder's heap

fixed_releases.verified_content: At netty-4.1.68.Final the decoder declares MAX_COMPRESSED_CHUNK_SIZE (16777216-1) and MAX_DECOMPRESSED_DATA_SIZE (65536); the effective protections read the Snappy preamble via snappy.getPreamble(in), reject an uncompressed size above 65536, allocate buffer(uncompressedSize, MAX_DECOMPRESSED_DATA_SIZE), and skip skippable chunks incrementally with numBytesToSkip. The MAX_COMPRESSED_CHUNK_SIZE comparison is vacuous for a 24-bit length.

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 is 7.5 High and the OSV/GHSA record carries the identical vector and HIGH label; the CNA publishes no numeric score. The legacy NVD CVSS v2 score is 5.0 Medium, an older metric version, not a same-version disagreement.

vulnerability.category_l2: Decompression: SnappyFrameDecoder accepts compressed chunks up to the 24-bit length field without a decompressed-size limit, and returns with a huge reserved-skippable chunk still buffered in the cumulation buffer

critical_operation.description: SnappyFrameDecoder.decode() reads the 24-bit chunkLength (line 96, getUnsignedMediumLE, so up to 16777215) and handles two memory-amplifying paths. RESERVED_SKIPPABLE (121-132): when fewer than 4 + chunkLength bytes are readable, decode() returns at line 128 and leaves the already-received chunk bytes in ByteToMessageDecoder's cumulation buffer (the in-code TODO on line 127 notes the bytes are kept), so a single huge skippable chunk is accumulated in full before it can be discarded. COMPRESSED_DATA (160-192): once 4 + chunkLength bytes are available the decoder skips to the Snappy payload, calls ctx.alloc().buffer() with no maximum (the default maxCapacity is Integer.MAX_VALUE), and calls snappy.decode(...) at lines 177 and 183 with no decompressed-size limit. Snappy.decode() then executes out.ensureWritable(uncompressedLength) (Snappy.java line 287), where readPreamble() (Snappy.java lines 363-379) accepts up to four varint bytes, i.e. a declared length up to 0x0FFFFFFF (268435455 bytes, about 256 MiB) that a tiny compressed frame can force the allocator to reserve. The merge commit 6da4956b adds numBytesToSkip streaming skips, a getPreamble() <= 65536 check and a bounded buffer(uncompressedSize, MAX_DECOMPRESSED_DATA_SIZE); its MAX_COMPRESSED_CHUNK_SIZE > 16777215 check is vacuous for a 24-bit length and is defense-in-depth only. CWE-400.

entry_point.description: An application installs a SnappyFrameDecoder in a Netty channel pipeline (or otherwise feeds it attacker-controlled bytes), and a remote client sends a Snappy stream containing a huge RESERVED_SKIPPABLE chunk or a COMPRESSED_DATA chunk whose decompressed size is far larger than the chunk.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA, NVD and both OSV record views agree on CWE-400 and on 4.1.68 as the first fixed release (CNA: lessThan 4.1.68Final; NVD: cpe versionEndExcluding 4.1.68; OSV GHSA endpoint: Maven ECOSYSTEM introduced 4.0.0, fixed 4.1.68.Final). NVD and the OSV/GHSA records publish the same CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH vector; the CNA publishes no numeric score, and NVD's additional CVSS 2.0 5.0 is a legacy metric version. OSV exposes two alias-linked records: the CVE endpoint carries a GIT range whose fixed event is the 4.1.68 release commit 7d34282f, while the GHSA endpoint carries the Maven ECOSYSTEM range; neither is a code fix. Local ancestry identifies the actual code fix as 6da4956b, first contained in netty-4.1.68.Final and absent from 4.1.66.Final, 4.1.67.Final and the 4.1.59.Final snapshot. GitHub's repository-scoped advisory metadata still reports medium with a null score, which is older than and contradicted by the global advisory/NVD/OSV records and is treated as stale metadata.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read SnappyFrameDecoder.decode at netty-4.1.59.Final and confirm there is no compressed-chunk or decompressed-size cap and that a partial reserved-skippable chunk is retained in the cumulation buffer.

An independent reviewer must confirm 6da4956b is the code fix, is not an ancestor of 4.1.59.Final or 4.1.67.Final and is contained in netty-4.1.68.Final, and that OSV's 7d34282f is the release commit.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range, the 4.1.68.Final fixed release and the CVSS 3.1 7.5 / CVSS 2.0 5.0 records.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
independent_corrections_accepted: Critical line range extended from 121-171 to 121-192 so it includes the actual decompression sink snappy.decode() at lines 177 and 183; the reviewer's range covers both the keep-buffering and allocation/decompression branches.

Affected range lower bound changed from >=0 to >=4.0.0 to match the OSV/GHSA Maven ECOSYSTEM range; the CNA and NVD omit a lower bound, and the GHSA record additionally lists io.netty:netty and org.jboss.netty:netty.

OSV was re-read per endpoint: the CVE-mapped record carries the GIT range fixed at release commit 7d34282f, while the GHSA endpoint carries the Maven ECOSYSTEM range 4.0.0 -> 4.1.68.Final. Both are now recorded as evidence, and the earlier single-record wording is superseded.

The decompression sink was documented precisely: Snappy.decode calls out.ensureWritable(uncompressedLength) at Snappy.java line 287, and readPreamble accepts up to four varint bytes (up to 0x0FFFFFFF, about 256 MiB), so a tiny frame can force a very large allocation.

The fix's MAX_COMPRESSED_CHUNK_SIZE > 16777215 check is vacuous because chunkLength is a 24-bit unsigned value; the effective protections are the 65536 decompressed-size cap and the streaming skip of skippable chunks.
GitHub's repository-scoped advisory shows medium/null while NVD, OSV and the global GitHub advisory agree on 7.5 HIGH; recorded as stale repository-level metadata rather than a severity disagreement.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier, now independently reviewed; grade B because no reproduction was executed.
No Netty pipeline, Snappy stream or heap-exhaustion measurement was executed; both amplification paths and the ~256 MiB declared-size figure are established statically.
Only the 4.1.59.Final vulnerable revision was diffed against 4.1.68.Final; intermediate releases and the other branches were not inspected individually.
The 4.0.0 lower bound comes from the OSV/GHSA Maven range; the CNA and NVD publish no lower bound, and trees below 4.1.59 were not individually diffed.
Impact requires an application to install SnappyFrameDecoder on a channel that receives attacker-controlled bytes; not every Netty deployment does so.
The fix's MAX_COMPRESSED_CHUNK_SIZE guard cannot trigger for a 24-bit chunkLength; the effective controls are the decompressed-size cap and streaming skips.
An incomplete COMPRESSED_DATA chunk is still retained in the cumulation buffer until complete, but that residual retention is bounded by the 24-bit chunk length (about 16 MiB).
GitHub's repository-scoped advisory metadata reports medium with a null score, older than and contradicted by NVD, OSV and the global advisory, and is treated as stale.
open_questions: Whether older 4.1.x or 4.0.x releases differ in the size of the buffered skippable chunk or in Snappy preamble handling was not audited.
Whether any pipeline-level frame-size limit commonly prevents reaching the decoder with a 16 MB chunk was not surveyed.
